Immunophenotype (CD31+, CD34+, D2‑40−) indicates blood‑vessel (not lymphatic) endothelium; Ki‑67 <1% supports a low‑proliferative (benign) process; HHV‑8 negativity argues strongly against Kaposi sarcoma. The salient histologic phrase “irregularly branched thin‑walled vessels dissecting through collagen” with hobnail/plump endothelial cells is classically described in hobnail (targetoid/hemosiderotic) hemangioma, and overlaps with other benign vascular tumors such as epithelioid hemangioma. Clinical course (young adult, slowly growing violaceous plaques confined to skin, no systemic symptoms) is most consistent with a benign cutaneous vascular tumor rather than an angiosarcoma or HHV‑8–driven lesion.

DIAGNOSIS:
1) Hobnail (targetoid/hemosiderotic) hemangioma — best fit histologically (thin‑walled, irregular branching vessels dissecting collagen; hobnail/plump endothelial cells; CD31+/CD34+, low Ki‑67).  
2) Epithelioid hemangioma (angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia) — similar plump/epithelioid endothelium and benign behavior; considered because of plaque/nodular vascular proliferation (would often have lobular architecture and eosinophils/inflammation).  
3) Tufted angioma / kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (benign/intermediate vascular proliferations) — can produce plaquelike vascular lesions in young adults; histology differs (tufts/“cannonball” aggregates) but still a reasonable alternative.  
4) Spindle cell (spindle‑cell) hemangioma — benign vascular tumor of young adults that can be multifocal and present on extremities; histology may show cavernous and spindle cell areas but can overlap immunophenotypically.  
5) Diffuse dermal angiomatosis / reactive vascular proliferation — can produce infiltrated erythematous plaques with diffuse dermal capillary proliferation; considered for plaque‑type lesions but usually associated with ischemic/underlying risk factors (absent here).

(Arguments against higher‑grade entities: Kaposi sarcoma is very unlikely given HHV‑8 negativity; cutaneous angiosarcoma is unlikely given lack of cytologic atypia and very low Ki‑67.)
